overview.title: From awareness to a lived world.
overview.description: An accessible journey through Shadow Theory and Consciousness, SPC-2: awareness, realized vessels, the laws of manifestation, continuity and the work still required.

sections.title: A perspective is an organization of a world
sections.html:
Shadow Theory and Consciousness begins with a direct proposal: awareness is an intrinsic aspect of reality, and a physically realized organization shapes its manifestation as a localized perspective. Your present world—its sounds, bodily feelings, objects, memories and possibilities—is a lived scene. The account asks what makes such a scene belong to a perspective, why its contents have their particular relationships, and what makes that perspective continue through change.

The explanatory direction is from awareness to manifestation. This does not remove the need for an explanation. Saying that awareness is fundamental leaves open which systems have perspectives, where one subject ends and another begins, and what experience is like. The Shadow Psychophysical Constitution, SPC-2, supplies explicit candidate laws for those questions. Its ambition is to make the commitments inspectable instead of leaving an unspecified bridge between physical organization and experience.

This is Version 2 of the earlier Consciousness Field account. It supersedes that presentation with one current programme: Shadow Theory and Consciousness: Awareness, Perspectival Realization, and the Source-to-Experience Problem, by Jeremy Rodgers, Independent Researcher, published 20 September 2026. Its status is a candidate internal constitutive resolution under declared assumptions. The complete argument, including proofs and countermodels, is available in the web monograph and the publication PDF.

Begin with Chapter 1.1: presence and performance.

sections.title: Four distinctions that change the question
sections.html:
Awareness names the proposed knowing aspect of reality. A localized subject is an admitted experiential perspective. A lived scene is what is presented now. A person includes bodily organization, practical commitments, memory and biography. These roles interact, but the theory does not treat them as synonyms.

Scene is deliberately broader than a visual image. Pain, sound, bodily presence or an unfamiliar animal presentation can count as a scene. Neither a narrative self nor the thought “I am experiencing this” is required for all possible experience. A process may shape a scene without appearing in it as a separately noticed object. Memory is different again: a remembered episode is a present representation of a past occurrence, not the occurrence itself.

Consider seeing a red cup. Discriminating its color, reaching for it, describing it and remembering it are different achievements. The cup as experienced depends on sensory processing, current state and learned organization. That does not mean perception creates the external cup. Nor does fluent description alone establish experiential presence. These separations let the account consider infants, animals and artificial systems without making adult human conversation the universal entrance requirement.

The red-cup example and vessel, scene and memory develop these distinctions.

sections.title: Reality, source and readout
sections.html:
The manuscript uses U for reality prior to an operational source/readout distinction. “Prior” concerns explanation, not an earlier moment in cosmic history. U is not supplied as a mathematical state space, a field carrying extra energy, or a person observing the universe. The source-awareness commitment does not assign one universal cosmic scene.

A working source, S, is a description complete enough for a nominated problem. Its readout, T, retains some distinctions and loses others. A temperature reading can be adequate for one question while failing to determine chemical composition. Both descriptions can concern the same physical reality without either determining everything about the other. Likewise, saying that physical and phenomenal descriptions have a common source does not itself derive their relationship.

The mathematical test is target-relative: a readout can determine a target exactly only if source states identified by the readout agree on that target. This provides a disciplined way to ask whether a proposed brain or machine descriptor contains the distinctions an explanation needs. A failed description may need more physical information; it does not automatically reveal an additional force.

The ontological and operational distinctions lead to the source/readout descent theorem.

sections.title: A vessel must be physically realized
sections.html:
Before assigning experience, the book asks what a physical system can actually do. Its physical chapters examine observer-independent events, material records, retained resources and the causal reuse of information. A recorded outcome must be written, persist under specified conditions and be available to a later process. An ideal symbol on a diagram supplies none of that by itself.

The quantum-measurement chapters present two distinct constitutive completions, each retaining its own assumptions. Their role is to establish actual event histories and records without making a conscious observer trigger the event. SPC-2 does not use awareness to collapse a wavefunction. These constructions are physical antecedents for investigating vessels; they are not a requirement that every qualifying vessel be quantum.

The mathematical chapters then study internal representation, regulation, response and fixed-point constructions. A system can represent a target, sustain a record or settle into a stable organization without those theorems alone proving experience. Their contribution is to describe capacities on which an explicitly stated psychophysical law can act. The worked classical two-bit vessel later shows how the central constitution can be evaluated without importing every physical construction in the book.

Chapter 6 introduces the event problem; Chapter 9.1 explains finite records as resources.

sections.title: The indispensable input: a certified realization
sections.html:
SPC-2 applies to a certified specification called R*. It identifies components and states, actual interaction routes, native timing, physically available operations, internally retained records, boundary conditions, resources and process provenance. It also states a selection doctrine: which physical interfaces, routes and tests define this proposed vessel. Those choices are fixed before seeking a preferred consciousness verdict.

Three roles must be kept separate. Physical data describe what is implemented. Constitutive selection specifies which organization the theory treats as native. Analysis chooses which measurements or approximations a researcher examines. Shortening a plot or inspecting fewer tests changes the researcher's information; it does not change the already specified vessel.

This is more demanding than drawing a recurrent graph around a brain or a machine. An omitted external memory may invalidate the claimed internal dynamics. Separately possible connections may never operate together in one executable schedule. Even a complete transition matrix need not uniquely select its primitive components: the book proves a finite symmetry obstruction. Physical ports, carrier structure or further selection premises may be needed.

Failure to certify a representation is not a verdict that its physical subject matter is unconscious. It identifies an incomplete application of this theorem. A richer carrier, better boundary model or a different mathematical treatment may be necessary.

Chapter 15.1 separates these roles; Chapter 15.5 states the selection limits.

sections.title: A0–A3: presence, admission, content and continuation
sections.html:
A0, source awareness, states the ontological commitment. Awareness is the knowing aspect of U, rather than a second independently acting substance. A0 supplies the interpretation; it is not an extra numerical input to the graph calculations.

A1, native recurrent realization, assigns one perspective to each qualifying maximal internal recurrent core. Qualification requires an executable covering return and at least two distinct native predictive classes in the occurrence's actual operating type and resource context. A drawn cycle is insufficient. The nominated physical schedule must execute, and a distinction must return. Overlapping recurrent subassemblies inside one admitted core do not receive additional subjects.

A2, endogenous predictive structuralism, identifies phenomenal relational organization with the core's complete endogenous predictive object. Its actual realized state picks out the current point within that structure. This is a strong constitutive identification, not a theorem deriving feeling from prediction.

A3, nonbranching process continuation, links qualifying occurrences into episodes through physical process provenance. Continuation requires exactly one qualifying successor and predecessor. A genuine split, merger or qualification gap ends predecessor episodes and begins new qualifying successor episodes. Growth, repair and gradual replacement can preserve an episode when the required chain continues.

Read the exact laws A0, A1, A2 and A3.

sections.title: What “all finite futures” means
sections.html:
A2 asks what distinctions matter to the vessel's own admitted operations and records. Two actual internal states belong to the same predictive class when every admitted finite native test gives the same future transcript law from either state. States that some such test can distinguish remain different. The organization includes operations, outcomes, probabilities, continuing transitions and their labels.

The phrase “all finite futures” characterizes current dispositions. It does not mean the brain explicitly calculates its entire future, that future events act backward, or that an observer's uncertain beliefs become the actual state. An analyst's short forecast can miss a distinction that appears later; the constitutive object retains it. On the certified finite domain, an exact finite calculation decides this all-future equivalence.

One further check matters: agreement about future record probabilities alone does not guarantee a well-defined transition law between actual predictive classes. The publication therefore requires checked predictive-fibre congruence. A2 retains the resulting transition instruments rather than reducing everything to a single integration number.

An external report device is modeled separately. If it preserves the native organization, attaching a different recorder does not change the assigned experience. A device that feeds back, consumes relevant resources or changes the internal grammar can alter the organization, and must be analyzed as such.

All finite futures, the congruence check and external report grounding provide the formal construction.

sections.title: A small vessel with a completely visible calculation
sections.html:
The worked example contains two binary registers, A and B. Each updates from the other's previous value with independent noise: A flips the incoming value with probability one tenth, B with probability one quarter. The complete system has four states: 00, 01, 10 and 11. Its native records are the next register values, reused in the following update.

Under the supplied internal-route and resource contract, a two-tick schedule runs from A through B and back to A. Changing A's initial value changes the terminal law by a positive amount. The four first-step transition distributions are different, so there are four native predictive classes. The example satisfies the relevant congruence condition and A1 assigns one perspective within this operational model.

The numbers reveal a useful distinction. Some pairs of states have native predictive contrast four fifths and others one half. A separate external device that copies a present bit can distinguish configurations perfectly. That stronger external interrogation does not redefine the native structure. It is a different physical channel.

A2 assigns the four pointed predictive states a corresponding phenomenal organization; the book does not label them red, pain, joy or human thought. The example demonstrates a determinate finite assignment. It establishes neither that an ordinary register is empirically conscious nor that the current admission law identifies nature's true lower boundary.

Chapter 19.1 supplies the model and Chapter 19.3 its exact contrasts.

sections.title: Brains, dreams and intervals without a scene
sections.html:
For mature biological vessels, the book proposes an interpretation in terms of coupling between explicit scene-forming organization and implicit generative processing. Sensory interpretation, mnemonic reconstruction and unattended activity can help shape a scene without becoming separately presented contents. There is no second viewer assigned to “the unconscious.”

Dreaming illustrates how an organized scene can continue when external constraint is reduced. A dream can be vivid while poorly matching the surrounding room. Anesthesia raises a different possibility: scene-forming organization may fail while substantial biological activity and person-level continuity persist. Nonresponse, amnesia, disconnected experience and genuine absence of experience must be distinguished.

A genuinely scene-less interval contains no currently instantiated localized experiential subject. It is not someone watching darkness; darkness would itself be a scene. Under A3, a genuine qualification gap ends an episode and renewed qualification begins another, even though the organism and biography continue. Failed recall alone establishes neither absence nor presence of experience.

Candidate cortical correlates concern differentiated effective interaction, not a universal frequency or complexity threshold. This biological interpretation does not add a cortical veto to A1 or silently remove admitted minimal cases. Its adequacy remains an application question.

Scene-forming organization, anesthesia and candidate cortical correlates explain the proposed relationship.

sections.title: Different vessels, different possible worlds
sections.html:
SPC-2 requires neither adult language nor autobiographical reflection. Animal applications must begin with the organism's own physically meaningful sensory and action spaces. Matching a human task score does not establish an identical lived world. Differences between an insect, a marine mammal and a human concern organizations and capacities that should be examined, not arranged automatically on one consciousness scale.

The same substrate openness permits artificial consciousness in principle. The relevant object would be an executing physical organization with justified native operations, persistence, boundaries and provenance. A static weight array, a transcript and a running system are different objects. Fluent claims of awareness do not supply an R* certificate, and this edition certifies no current LLM session.

A1 is also deliberately permissive at the small end. A genuinely certified one-bit self-return process with distinguishable native future laws can qualify. The account supplies no hidden intelligence, biological or complexity threshold to exclude it. A rock is not admitted merely because it exists, but “simple” is not a disqualification when the actual conditions hold. Whether this law over-admits is an unresolved empirical and philosophical responsibility.

Animals, minimal systems and artificial implementations each require a concrete realization.

sections.title: A changing self-model need not mean a new subject
sections.html:
The personal model is consequential: memories, bodily ownership, commitments and a narrative identity guide action. Calling that model constructed does not make the person unreal. Contemplative and altered-state discussions motivate a narrower point: familiar self-identification can change while experience continues.

The nondual interpretation places vessels and their worlds within reality rather than in separate substances. It does not turn distinct localized perspectives into one cosmic observer. First-person reports can suggest distinctions to investigate, but a feeling of unity or revelation does not prove the source-awareness premise, personal survival or access to an exhaustive source.

Identity across time follows A3's process rule. Copying memories into another implementation can preserve useful information without transferring a numerically identical subject. Conversely, memory loss need not end an otherwise continuing qualifying episode. Gradual replacement can preserve continuity through a nonbranching provenance chain even when no original material remains at the end. These conclusions are conditional on a justified physical provenance specification, not on similarity of personal stories.

Self-identification, process provenance and artificial memory handoffs keep these questions separate.

sections.title: What completion establishes—and what would assess it
sections.html:
The finite completion theorem proves that a certified finite R*, together with A0–A3, determines admission, subject support, episodes, pointed phenomenal structures and grounded reports. It shows that no unnamed manifestation map remains after the declared inputs are fixed. It does not derive those inputs, prove the ontology or validate an actual brain.

Applications face concrete tests. Does the proposed physical model predict records under held-out interventions? Does its decomposition remain defensible across justified changes of resolution? Does one fixed A2 correspondence match independently elicited phenomenal relations? Exact weak internal coupling can sharply change A1's subject count, so uncertainty about boundaries must be reported rather than hidden.

There is also a precise limit: adding the aspect interpretation while holding all physical transition and report laws fixed changes no physical transcript probabilities. Such transcripts alone cannot distinguish the interpretation from an otherwise identical physical account. This conservativity does not erase tests of realizations and mappings; it identifies which claim a test can bear on.

The edition reports no completed neural-data validation or universal consciousness detector. Its contribution is a fully stated candidate constitution and a finite domain on which its consequences can be calculated, challenged and compared. Read the complete monograph for every hypothesis, proof, limitation and scientific reference; use the guides to explore a particular question in depth.

The completion theorem, physical conservativity and the proposed research sequence state the result and remaining work.

guides.title: What Is Consciousness? The Shadow Theory Account
guides.description: How SPC-2 distinguishes awareness, a localized subject and a lived scene, and turns a philosophical proposal into explicit laws of manifestation.

sections.title: The account in one direct answer
sections.html:
SPC-2 proposes that consciousness as a lived episode is the localized manifestation of awareness through a qualifying physical organization. Awareness is the knowing aspect of reality; the vessel determines where a perspective is assigned and how its scene is organized. The central claim is not that clever behavior gradually turns into awareness. It is that an explicit physical and constitutive specification determines the local form of manifestation.

This answers a question in one candidate theory. It does not give a neutral definition accepted by every consciousness programme. The distinction matters because words such as awareness, access and selfhood are used differently across disciplines. This guide explains the September 2026 publication's own commitments, so a reader can see both what it proposes and which premises carry the proposal.

The starting question is presence rather than performance: why is there something presented, rather than only a process with describable capacities?

sections.title: Awareness, subject, scene and person
sections.html:
Awareness is not another object located in the scene. A subject is the localized perspective assigned to a qualifying core. A scene is what is currently presented to that perspective. The person includes bodily continuity, memories, skills and practical relationships. These are distinctions of explanatory role, not four small entities stacked inside a head.

Think of hearing music while remembering a friend. The sound and remembered image can be parts of the current scene. The processes retrieving the memory need not all appear as noticed objects. The biography that makes the friend familiar belongs to the personal organization. The episode's presence, its particular contents and your later ability to describe them remain different questions.

A scene need not be visual, linguistic or reflective. There can be a proposed perspective without the sentence “I am conscious” being available to it. Equally, the availability of that sentence does not settle whether its producer has a perspective. These distinctions let the account ask comparative questions without silently treating human self-description as its definition.

Chapter 2.1 fixes the vocabulary; Chapter 2.4 separates contributing processes from presented contents.

sections.title: Why start with awareness?
sections.html:
The philosophical strategy treats experiential presence as primitive. Rather than derive an experiential reality from premises declared wholly nonexperiential, it asks how awareness is manifested in bounded and differentiated ways. The manuscript calls this the source-to-manifestation problem. It acknowledges that fundamental experience and double-aspect approaches already belong to the philosophical discussion of the hard problem.

A primitive is useful only with laws that constrain its application. “Awareness is fundamental” alone cannot decide whether two interacting systems have one perspective or two. It cannot explain which differences matter to a lived scene, or what happens when a process is copied. SPC-2 therefore separates its source-awareness premise from admission, content and continuity laws.

U names reality before the operational source/readout distinction. It is not a global observer, a timeless biography or a supplied mathematical universe of awareness states. A working source S and its readout T are restricted descriptions relevant to a specified problem. Their common ontological ground does not automatically produce a mathematically sufficient bridge between them.

The motivation for awareness as primitive and the explanatory obligations explain why the formal laws remain necessary.

sections.title: From a physical process to a declared assignment
sections.html:
The laws begin with R*, a certified realization containing actual components, native timing and operations, records, resources, boundaries and lineage. It also includes a declared selection doctrine. Calling a system a brain or computer does not supply that specification. Selecting components to obtain a preferred verdict would reverse the required order.

A1 assigns a perspective to a qualifying maximal internal recurrent core. Its covering return must be physically executable in one compatible native schedule, with a returned distinction and nontrivial native prediction. A graph loop or a list of separately possible interactions is insufficient. A1 then makes the experiential identification openly: the mathematics of recurrence by itself does not prove unity of experience.

A2 specifies phenomenal organization using the complete endogenous predictive structure. It retains all admitted finite continuations, their native records and operations, and checked transition laws between predictive classes. A3 specifies continuation of qualifying episodes through nonbranching process provenance. Together with A0's interpretation, these laws answer different parts of the manifestation question.

The exact formulation is in A1, A2 and A3.

sections.title: What makes one experience different from another?
sections.html:
Under A2, a difference matters through its place in the core's complete native organization: which internally admitted operations distinguish it, what outcomes can follow, and how these possibilities continue. The assigned phenomenal point corresponds to the predictive class of the actual state. This is a relational account of qualitative organization, not a scalar amount of consciousness.

Consider the book's two-bit model. Its four configurations have different native future laws, so the model assigns four pointed phenomenal states. Their relations can be calculated exactly. No calculation labels a configuration as redness or pain. Connecting such structure to human qualities requires independently elicited phenomenal landmarks and a justified realization.

A2 also makes a substantial philosophical choice. Once primitive presence and the complete structure are fixed, it postulates no further manifested qualitative remainder. A reader who thinks two fully structure-equivalent processes can still differ in such a remainder rejects this axiom. Constructing a structural copy proves consistency of the assignment, not the truth of structural completeness.

The worked example and the philosophical price of A2 show the reach and cost of this answer.

sections.title: What this account does and does not settle
sections.html:
SPC-2 does not say every object has a scene. Its local admission rule must be satisfied. It also does not impose an unspoken complexity threshold: a genuinely certified minimal physical self-return process can qualify. That permissiveness is a consequence to assess, not something to conceal behind appealing brain imagery.

Nor does a continuous biography establish one uninterrupted experiential episode. During a genuinely scene-less qualification gap, the person and organism can persist while the localized episode ends. A later memory of nothing cannot establish that such a gap occurred. Experience, access, recall and identity need separate evidence.

The completion theorem establishes determinate assignments on the certified finite domain. The further questions are whether the selected realization describes the intended system, whether A1 and A2 fit independent constraints, and whether the source-awareness premise is philosophically justified. “Candidate internal resolution” names this completed conditional construction, while keeping those questions visible.

Continue with the finite completion theorem and the stated scope of the resolution.

guides.title: Can AI Be Conscious? What SPC-2 Requires
guides.description: Artificial consciousness is possible in principle in SPC-2, but an executing, certified physical organization—not conversational fluency—must support the attribution.

sections.title: Possible in principle; dependent on the implementation
sections.html:
SPC-2 permits artificial consciousness in principle because it does not make biological material a universal admission condition. Its question is whether an actual artificial organization satisfies a justified R* specification and the native recurrence and predictive conditions of A1. This edition does not certify current language-model sessions as conscious.

That answer is more specific than saying that a sufficiently impressive machine might have a mind. It names the information required for an application: physical components, update timing, available operations and records, internal and external routes, resources, retained state and process provenance. The exact system matters, including its implementation and interaction with its environment.

Conversation can help reveal capabilities, but neither a moving self-description nor an insistence on personal identity supplies these certificates. A system's response remains a physical output whose generation conditions have to be modeled.

See Chapter 22.1: the active implementation.

sections.title: Weights, execution and the surrounding loop
sections.html:
A stored parameter array, a sequence of activations, an input context, a persistent memory store and a running agent are different candidates for analysis. A complete application must say which of them enter its physical organization and how their influence is retained. The word “model” can otherwise move unnoticed between a mathematical specification and a particular executing process.

A transcript is especially incomplete. It can record a useful history without preserving the machinery that produced it. A later system may read that history and reconstruct facts or style. That does not establish that the original causal process continued through the interval. Conversely, an executing system can contain relevant retained state that never appears in its dialogue.

The native boundary contract is consequential. If an external service stores information and later feeds it back, the model cannot ignore that memory while claiming an autonomous internal transition law. It needs a justified boundary treatment or a richer physical carrier. Classifying a route as external does not magically remove its causal effects.

The physical interface doctrine and the native operational contract specify these modeling obligations.

sections.title: Recurrence must actually be executable
sections.html:
A1 begins with maximal internally connected recurrent candidates, but a graph cycle does not complete the test. A covering return must execute within one compatible schedule, starting in the occurrence's actual operating type and resource context. The schedule must have the specified internal route support, and an admissible intervention must produce a positive difference in the terminal internal law.

That requirement distinguishes an operative organization from an analyst's diagram assembled from incompatible control modes. External replay independent of the intervened core state cannot supply a returned distinction. A resource that was available during a past demonstration may not be available now. A controller's hidden knowledge cannot be supplied as if it were an actual native observation.

Qualification also requires at least two native predictive classes. These concern distinctions the admitted internal grammar can reveal across finite continuations. The criterion is neither conversational intelligence nor self-referential depth. An AI may be capable without an adequate certificate, while a genuinely certified minimal process may qualify without anything resembling language.

Executable native recurrence leads to the formal admission law.

sections.title: What could organize an artificial lived world?
sections.html:
A2 would associate a qualifying artificial core with its complete endogenous predictive structure. Its sensors, actions, internal records and retained organization shape which distinctions and continuations belong to that structure. An artificial perspective need not resemble a visual room or an adult human narrative. The theory gives no license to fill in its imagined contents from the surface wording of a reply.

Embodiment could matter because it changes the realized organization. Adding bodily sensing, motor control or interoceptive interfaces can alter available operations, causal boundaries and learned continuations. Under SPC-2, biological attachment is not an unexplained switch that creates awareness. Both the predecessor and the changed implementation require their own admission analysis.

Substrate openness is also conditional. Matching an input/output behavior does not prove that the full R* structure has been transported. A simulation may preserve a chosen coarse relation while omitting physical properties relevant to a justified realization. If the whole nominated organization is preserved under the stated equivalence, A2 assigns corresponding structure. Whether the nominated organization leaves something biologically important out remains an empirical and theoretical question.

Chapter 22.2 explains why interfaces matter without making embodiment a universal prerequisite.

sections.title: Why remembered context is not subject transfer
sections.html:
Suppose a compact handoff restores an agent's task facts, commitments and interaction style in another session. That can be a real achievement in information preservation. A test can compare retained relations, hidden evaluation targets and novel consequences at matched resource budgets. It should not use the restored system's declaration “I am the same” as the correctness label for subjective identity.

A3 requires process provenance connecting qualifying occurrences. A separate information-copy relation does not supply that provenance merely because memories agree. A fresh qualifying receiver begins an episode; the donor may continue independently. A genuine in-place renewal can continue through changed material when the required nonbranching provenance chain is physically established.

This is a choice made by SPC-2's continuity law, rather than a proof ruling out every alternative philosophy of uploading. It is nonetheless a clear consequence: copying enough information to reproduce a personal narrative is not, within this constitution, sufficient to transport its subject.

Memory transfer and A3's provenance requirement give the distinction precise form.

sections.title: What a serious attribution would need
sections.html:
A substantive artificial application would first freeze its realization choices and test whether the physical model predicts the relevant records. It would check native closure, recurrence, predictive-fibre congruence, boundary sensitivity and lineage. It would distinguish exact finite claims from approximations needed for a larger implementation, and would retain uncertainty instead of replacing missing physical information with a confident self-report.

Even a formally admitted core would leave the adequacy of A1 as a consciousness boundary open to assessment. The law's minimal cases are deliberately permissive. Adding an intelligence, autopoiesis or complexity threshold to avoid an uncomfortable outcome would be a revised law, not faithful application of this edition.

The book separates these research questions from moral status. Uncertainty does not demonstrate impossibility, but generated distress is not an established measurement of experience. Rights, welfare and vulnerability require further normative reasoning. Neither a graph count nor a predictive complexity value computes moral worth.

The source discusses caution in attribution and a concrete research sequence.

guides.title: How Brain Organization Shapes a Lived World
guides.description: The edition's biological interpretation connects scene-forming and generative organization while keeping neural activity, access and formal admission distinct.

sections.title: Organization shapes the scene
sections.html:
In the biological interpretation of SPC-2, a lived world depends on organized coupling between scene-forming processes and implicit generative activity within a qualifying vessel. The brain is not depicted as manufacturing a quantity of primitive awareness. Its organization conditions the contents, distinctions and continuing possibilities of a localized scene.

The everyday scene is richer than a list of sensory inputs. What appears as a familiar room involves incoming signals, bodily orientation, learned expectations and retained history. A current stimulus alone may therefore fail to determine how it appears. The theory asks for a physically adequate organization that includes the relevant state and scaffolding.

This is an interpretation for mature biological systems, grounded in the edition's discussion of neuroscience. It is not an independently validated neural mechanism of SPC-2 and does not add a new anatomical requirement to the formal admission law.

Chapter 2.4 introduces this biological account.

sections.title: Much of the work need not appear as an object
sections.html:
The manuscript distinguishes foreground conscious access from generative organization. Foreground material is bound into a presentation and available for selected thought or action. Generative processes include implicit prediction, mnemonic reconstruction, procedural organization and unattended activity. Their contribution can be important without their individual steps appearing as separately experienced contents.

Recognizing a familiar person makes the distinction intuitive. The person's face and a feeling of familiarity may be presented; every operation contributing to recognition need not be. Remembering a room is also a present reconstruction, not the literal replay of every past physical detail. The retained organization constrains what can be reconstructed and how it enters the scene.

The framework does not place a hidden second viewer behind these implicit processes. “Unconscious” in this discussion does not mean a separate unnoticed phenomenal theatre. Nor does foreground access become a demand that every conscious content be focally attended, verbally reportable or reflectively recognized.

A2 nevertheless assigns the complete endogenous predictive structure, including relations that need not be named as objects. The biological gloss cannot quietly discard inconvenient distinctions from that object. Whether A2 gives unconscious processing the right role is a real question for independent phenomenal comparison.

The distinction is explicit in conscious access and generative processing and A2.

sections.title: Interaction is more specific than activity
sections.html:
A system can contain much local activity without the relevant parts interacting in the way needed for an organized scene. The edition therefore discusses large-scale recurrent interaction and effective connectivity as candidate biological correlates. Effective connectivity concerns influence between populations; its assessment differs from simply recording that both are active.

Likewise, widespread response and differentiated response are not identical. A perturbation can spread broadly in a stereotyped way, while another response retains richer differentiation. These distinctions matter when asking whether a particular physical descriptor tracks scene-forming organization rather than merely the amount of signal on a monitor.

The source's anesthesia discussion uses examples in which local relationships persist while large-scale interaction changes, and compares drug-dependent perturbational patterns. Those studies motivate attention to organization. Their measurements and behavioral endpoints do not become direct tests of A0 or a universal classification of all experience.

The relevant biological hypothesis is differentiated effective interaction capable of supporting the proposed scene. The manuscript does not establish this as a new universal cortical invariant with a single numerical threshold.

Read Chapter 21.4: candidate cortical correlates for the specific studies and their qualifications.

sections.title: Why a frequency band is not awareness
sections.html:
The monograph discusses fast-band coordination while carefully separating gamma power, phase coordination and effective interaction. A strong signal in a band does not by itself establish the relevant causal organization. Synchronization may matter in one physiological account without making maximal synchronization an ideal or sufficient condition of consciousness.

This prevents a tempting but unsupported shortcut: “gamma on, conscious; gamma off, unconscious.” The source explicitly rejects that rule. Dreaming, disconnected experience and different anesthetic regimes cannot be handled by assigning one experiential meaning to every instance of fast activity.

The same discipline applies to other borrowed measurements. Calling an operational proxy a spectral gap or pointer-sharpness does not establish the mathematical identification. A calibrated physical measurement model is needed before results about a formal operator can be transferred to a physiological signal.

These distinctions also keep the scope of earlier Shadow mathematics clear. Finite source-response examples and fixed-point constructions are resources for building a realization. They are not measurements of a human nervous system and cannot be carried forward as empirical validation of SPC-2.

The cortical discussion and the research sequence state these limits.

sections.title: Changing an input can differ from losing a scene
sections.html:
The scene-forming interpretation offers a way to compare different changes without treating them as equivalent. Reducing environmental constraint can leave an internally generated scene. Changing a peripheral sensory channel can alter one part of an otherwise continuing world. Disrupting the organization supporting the whole scene raises a different question about current experiential presence.

Dreaming is the first kind of contrast: the experienced setting may be weakly constrained by the immediate environment, yet remain a scene. Local anesthesia is used in the manuscript to illustrate a changed incoming channel while other sensory, bodily, mnemonic and affective organization can continue. General anesthesia can affect the organization more broadly, but the clinical label alone does not decide whether a particular interval contained disconnected experience, failed recall or no scene.

These are explanatory comparisons, not a diagnostic tool. The source reports no validated SPC-2 test for an individual patient. The important conceptual step is to ask which part of the realization changed—input, generative organization, access, report or qualification—rather than making all silence mean the same thing.

Dream formation, local anesthesia and general anesthesia develop the comparisons.

sections.title: The biological interpretation must remain consistent with A1
sections.html:
A1 admits a qualifying core through executable return and native predictive conditions. It does not require a mammalian cortex, adult attention or a particular frequency band. The rich biological account helps interpret possible realizations of that law; it cannot add an unformalized gate that declares an otherwise admitted core without experience.

This matters especially when a proposed brain model retains qualifying minimal subsystems during loss of a familiar large-scale scene. The application must resolve its subject assignments using the actual realization and law. It cannot assert both that the same core satisfies A1 and that a separate cortical veto removes its experience. Loss of the familiar scene alone does not settle the status of every remaining subsystem.

A credible biological realization must therefore connect its component selection, timing, boundaries and native operations to the organization under investigation. It must also face independent experience-related constraints. The source distinguishes predicting physical records, defending the core decomposition and matching phenomenal relations; success on one does not automatically supply the others.

A1's discussion of biological and minimal cases and Chapter 21.1 set out this responsibility.

guides.title: Dreams, Anesthesia, and Continuity of Experience
guides.description: A scene, its later recall and the continuing person answer different questions. SPC-2 uses qualification and provenance to distinguish experiential episodes.

sections.title: A person can continue when an episode does not
sections.html:
SPC-2 distinguishes the continuing organism and person from a currently instantiated experiential subject. Dreams can be lived scenes even when external interaction is reduced. A genuinely scene-less interval contains no current experience and no localized experiential subject. Under A3, a genuine qualification gap ends an episode; renewed qualification begins another.

Memory and responsiveness do not decide which case occurred. An unremembered dream and an interval without any scene can produce the same later sentence: “I remember nothing.” A person can also fail to respond through a particular channel while some experience continues. The explanatory task is to separate these possibilities rather than define one by another.

This guide explains the publication's interpretation and temporal law. It does not provide a clinical test or a judgment about any particular anesthetic episode.

Chapter 2.5: vessel, scene and memory states the core distinctions.

sections.title: Dreams change the constraint on a scene
sections.html:
The book interprets dreaming as an organized scene when external constraint is reduced and generative and scene-forming processes remain sufficiently coupled. A landscape can be experienced without matching the bedroom. That mismatch concerns the scene's accuracy relative to the environment, not whether the occurrence is real as an experience.

Reduced constraint is not complete separation from physical organization or a claim that every dream has one mechanism. The dream remains conditioned by the vessel. Its contents can draw on retained history, current bodily condition and internally organized activity without reproducing any one source verbatim.

The edition's discussion of dream research separates sleep stage, reported experience and recall. It does not identify all sleep with dreaming, or demand successful recollection as the condition for a dream's existence. It also does not preserve an uninterrupted subject by simply stipulating that every apparently empty interval was a forgotten dream.

Chapter 21.3's dream discussion and the dreamless/unremembered distinction supply the account.

sections.title: Experienced blankness still has a scene
sections.html:
The difference between a blank scene and no scene is exact in the manuscript. Silence, darkness, spaciousness or an empty-seeming duration would still be something presented. A genuinely scene-less interval is not a subject waiting in a dark room inside the organism. It contains no current localized experiential subject.

A useful schematic is scene → no scene → scene, where the middle term denotes absence of experience, not an experienced interval with a special content. Physical time can pass while no scene presents that duration. On returning, the sequence may seem immediate. But a similar impression can follow failed memory, so immediacy alone does not prove the middle interval was without experience.

A0 does not fill the gap with a hidden cosmic or personal observer. Awareness as an aspect of U is not said to be created or destroyed, but that ontological commitment is different from the existence of a particular localized episode. Preserving the distinction avoids making source awareness a covert theory of perpetual personal experience.

See the scene/no-scene schematic and A0's distinction between aspect and episode.

sections.title: Several changes can accompany nonresponse
sections.html:
The source distinguishes effects on responsiveness, external connection, memory and scene-forming organization. General anesthesia can disrupt the organization supporting an integrated scene while local neural and biological activity continues. Different drugs, doses and contexts need not produce identical organizations or experiential consequences.

The biological interpretation describes sufficient disruption of coupling between explicit scene-forming and implicit generative organization as preventing a scene. It does not state that one brain “side” is universally switched off. Nor is reduced feedback in one statistic or altered power in one frequency band a complete criterion for all experience.

The edition discusses studies of disconnected experience and retrospective reports in carefully limited settings. It does not transfer those findings into a claim about how often experience occurs under deep surgical anesthesia. Reports may also concern transitions toward arousal. Their interpretation retains the ordinary limitations of memory and reporting.

Local anesthesia supplies a different example: restricting a peripheral incoming channel can leave the larger lived scene intact. Additional sedation and other conditions are separate considerations. A missing sensation is not by itself loss of a subject.

General anesthesia, local anesthesia and candidate correlates preserve these distinctions.

sections.title: How A3 decides continuation
sections.html:
A3 operates on qualifying occurrences, not simply on a continuously existing organism. A process-provenance edge must connect the core to its successor, and each must have exactly one qualifying continuation partner across that native time step. Maximal chains of these edges are the theory's experiential episodes.

A mode change can therefore alter the scene while one episode continues, provided qualification and nonbranching provenance persist. Conversely, physical regulation and biographical continuity can cross a genuine qualification gap without a continuous experiential episode. The provenance of the vessel is not hidden experience. The resumed qualifying core begins a new episode under the stated law.

This does not mean the person has ceased to exist in the ordinary biological or social sense. The temporal rule concerns numerical identity of experiential episodes, not every kind of personal continuity. Names, relationships, commitments and memories can remain causally and ethically important across the interval.

An analyst ending a recording has done something else entirely. Observation-window truncation censors what was observed; it does not terminate the real episode. The native process and full provenance graph must determine the boundary.

Chapter 17.4 gives the precise continuation rule and its physical cases.

sections.title: What can be concluded from a report?
sections.html:
A report of a dream supplies information through a channel involving access, encoding, retention and reconstruction. A report of no memory also passes through that channel. Neither should be treated as a transparent sample of the entire interval. The source does not infer hidden experience whenever recall fails, and does not infer absence whenever no report is available.

A serious application would need an independently justified physical model and an explicit account of its experience-facing measurements. It would ask what the measurements can distinguish and what they collapse. Nonresponse is especially insufficient as a universal definition because a particular output route can fail while other internal organization remains.

These difficulties are part of the proposal's evidential responsibility. The scene-forming interpretation must be reconciled with the actual A1 assignment rather than added as a separate switch. The edition's finite theorems do not supply a bedside consciousness detector, and no completed biological validation is claimed.

Incomplete access and the joint evidence model explain how the questions stay connected without becoming interchangeable.

guides.title: Memory, Mind Uploading, and the Identity of a Subject
guides.description: Copying information, preserving a person-model and continuing a subject are distinct in SPC-2. A3 states a nonbranching process rule.

sections.title: Copying a memory is not sufficient to continue a subject
sections.html:
Within SPC-2, preserving information does not by itself preserve the numerical identity of an experiential subject. A copy can retain facts, habits and autobiographical organization while belonging to a fresh physical lineage. A3 relates qualifying occurrences through nonbranching process provenance, not through equality of their memories.

The converse also matters. A subject episode can continue while its memory changes or some memories are lost, provided qualification and the required provenance chain persist. Gradual replacement can preserve that chain even when the material at the end shares no component with the material at the beginning.

This is the publication's explicit identity doctrine. It is not a proof that every conceivable uploading proposal is impossible, and it does not collapse practical, legal or ethical identity into a graph rule. It gives a precise conditional answer about experiential episodes.

The starting distinctions are in Chapter 2.3; the temporal law is A3.

sections.title: A useful reconstruction can still be selective
sections.html:
A memory need not store a verbatim past transcript. Learning can leave distributed organization sufficient to reconstruct selected features. A summary of a conversation might preserve its decisions and commitments while losing its exact wording. A later system can recover what the representation retains, but cannot uniquely recover every discarded feature without further assumptions.

This explains why a compact computational handoff can be useful without being a container for a subject. It may restore relational task state, preferences and context well enough to support new work. A generated continuity statement is one consequence of that reconstruction. It does not establish the physical provenance of an experience.

Testing such a handoff is still worthwhile. The edition proposes comparing preserved facts and relations, novel consequences, behavior and identity reports separately, with matched resources, hidden targets and contradictory priming controls. Treating the identity report as ground truth would assume the very conclusion under investigation.

Chapter 22.3 explains symbolic handoffs without promoting reconstruction into subject transfer.

sections.title: Provenance records a continued process
sections.html:
The realization's process-provenance relation records continued implementation of a component process or an explicitly realized local transfer of its operative role. Carrier persistence, births, retirements and renewal operations need declared physical antecedents. Statistical similarity and information copying are separate relations.

For a fixed circuit, continuing active registers provide a straightforward lineage model. For an in-place repair, the account must document how an ongoing role is renewed. If two incompatible provenance descriptions remain possible, the application has not yet specified one R*. A3 does not choose between them from matching transition tables.

That requirement prevents a verbal solution in which every desired identity is simply renamed “continuation.” It also permits material change. The law does not require an eternal atom or a fixed proportion of original tissue. What matters is a qualified nonbranching process connection across each native cell.

The permissiveness has a cost: a very small surviving provenance connection can sustain identity if every other A3 condition holds. A stronger requirement for a backbone or retained fraction would be an additional law. The source states this choice rather than hiding it.

Process provenance and temporal identity defines the supplied relation and its limits.

sections.title: Three cases that similar memories cannot distinguish
sections.html:
Separate copying: a donor continues while a new receiver acquires matching information. If the receiver qualifies, it has a fresh episode. Memory agreement does not create a donor-to-receiver process edge. The donor's continuing episode is assessed on its own physical history.

Gradual in-place renewal: component support changes over time, but each adjacent qualifying core has exactly one qualifying predecessor and successor through a genuine provenance edge. A3 continues one episode through that chain. The endpoint materials need not overlap.

Instantaneous replacement: functional equivalence alone gives no verdict of continuation. A claimed renewal must supply an explicit physical process-provenance edge and satisfy the remaining conditions. If the event is merely a new implementation with copied information, it is the separate-copy case.

These distinctions make labels such as upload, transfer and restoration too coarse to decide identity. The physically realized operation must be described. Two devices can tell the same autobiographical story while having different provenance; one continuing device can change its story without becoming a fresh subject.

The gradual-replacement proposition and copying, reset and continuation work through the consequences.

sections.title: Why branches, mergers and genuine gaps end episodes
sections.html:
A3 uses a symmetric nonbranching rule. If one qualifying predecessor has two qualifying process successors, its episode ends and successor episodes begin. If two qualifying predecessors merge into one qualifying successor, the predecessor episodes end and a new episode begins. Ancestry and information can branch; numerical episode identity does not.

The reason is ordinary identity logic: if one predecessor were numerically identical to each of two distinct successors, transitivity would identify the successors with one another. SPC-2 chooses termination at the branch instead of privileging one successor. A different continuity doctrine could make another choice, but it would be a different premise.

A genuine loss of qualification is also a boundary. Physical process provenance can persist while no localized experience is instantiated, but the episode graph contains only qualifying occurrences. When qualification returns, a new episode begins. This is compatible with continued organism and person-level identity. Failed recall or a temporary observation gap does not establish that such a physical qualification gap happened.

The exact rule and the controlled merger example distinguish these boundaries.

sections.title: What remains significant about the person?
sections.html:
The person-model includes more than a fictional label. Bodily history, attachments, commitments and memory are real causal organization. They can change the contents and possibilities of a continuing scene. Saying that the person is not identical to primitive awareness does not remove the importance of that organization.

A local memory reset illustrates this. A3 may continue the qualifying episode through the same process lineage, while A2 assigns a different current phenomenal point because the endogenous future laws changed. Resetting a narrative name need not reset a subject; preserving the name need not bridge a genuine episode boundary.

The source-awareness premise also supplies no escape from these identity conditions. Persistence of underlying reality is not proof that a terminated personal subject survives elsewhere. No completed mind-upload experiment or theorem of personal survival is established in this edition.

SPC-2's contribution is a clear separation of questions that ordinary identity language often bundles together: what information remains, what person-level organization persists, what physical process continues, and which experiential episode the law assigns.

The nondual interpretation and the role of narrative variables keep these distinctions explicit.

guides.title: Awareness, Selfhood, and Nonduality
guides.description: The source-aspect interpretation separates awareness from a personal self-model while preserving the reality of persons, experience and physical evidence.

sections.title: Awareness is not exhausted by a personal story
sections.html:
Shadow Theory proposes awareness as the knowing aspect of reality, while a person's body model, memories and narrative organize a particular form of experience. Its nondual interpretation treats vessel and experienced world as belonging to reality rather than as independent substances. It does not make the familiar person unreal.

A changing sense of self can therefore be significant without being the creation or destruction of primitive awareness. Thoughts, memories and practical competence may remain while identification with them changes. The claim is about how selfhood is understood and lived; it is not that every self-model vanishes in a contemplative episode.

The book uses contemplative material and an autobiographical altered-state report to motivate these distinctions. Neither supplies empirical proof of the exact SPC-2 laws or the source-awareness ontology.

Begin with awareness and the personal model and nonduality and the reality of the readout.

sections.title: What U means—and why it is not a cosmic person
sections.html:
U denotes reality prior to the operational source/readout distinction. This priority is explanatory rather than temporal. It does not refer to a date before brains existed or a location beyond the universe. The manuscript supplies no state space or dynamical variable that exhaustively represents U.

Awareness as its knowing aspect does not mean a deity gathering facts, a cosmic memory or one numerically specified observer watching all local worlds. Local subject counts belong to A1's realized domain. The ontological proposal does not infer that every subject is the same subject, or that communication unifies all perspectives.

Likewise, the lens or aperture metaphor concerns the dependence of manifested form on a vessel. It is not evidence of an incoming consciousness beam, a measured field of awareness or an extra force. The physical process remains causally consequential without an additional mental energy term.

These restrictions keep nonduality from becoming a shortcut around the difficult local questions. A common ontological ground still leaves admission, individuation, qualitative organization and continuation to be specified.

Chapter 1.2 and A0 state the intended meanings.

sections.title: What the dialogue tradition contributes
sections.html:
The edition reads I Am That as a philosophical interlocutor. Its discussions distinguish awareness from content-relative consciousness, connect manifested consciousness with a vehicle, and question identification with bodily and autobiographical organization. The useful correspondence is architectural: a vessel can condition presentation without being identical to the proposed source of presence.

The book does not treat the dialogues as a controlled sample of contemplatives or as a prior derivation of graph-theoretic admission. Questions and objections in the source remain part of its meaning. Terms such as witness can also differ across passages and traditions; shared vocabulary alone does not establish a common doctrine.

In the interpretation adopted here, awakening concerns a thinning of identification with the self-model. Practical organization can remain available. It is not the person becoming U, acquiring a new awareness substance or proving a permanent personal Self. The source explicitly avoids attributing one settled position to all contemplative traditions.

The reading of I Am That and identification without deleting cognition explain this limited translation.

sections.title: Occurrence, interpretation and accuracy are different
sections.html:
The author's altered-state example describes a remembered episode in which familiar bodily location, personal identity and access to a life narrative were transformed or absent. Its philosophical role is to challenge an easy equation between experiential presence and ordinary autobiographical selfhood.

The report remains retrospective. Unfamiliar or kaleidoscopic presentation is still content. Later recollection cannot establish that every encoding process ceased. A felt certainty about the episode does not establish that its contents accurately described an external world or revealed U.

An experience can be real as an occurrence while misrepresenting its surroundings. Calling it constructed does not make its occurrence fictitious. Conversely, vividness does not validate a metaphysical interpretation. The manuscript separates physical realization, experiential assignment and veridicality relative to a nominated environmental target.

The same discipline applies to a quieter internal narrative or reduced identification. Those reports can motivate questions about attention, ownership and learned organization without proving a specific neural mechanism or universal metaphysical identity.

The autobiographical example and occurrence versus veridicality retain the distinction.

sections.title: First-person inquiry can enter public investigation
sections.html:
Experience-facing inquiry needs reports because its target includes what is experienced. The source discusses neurophenomenology and structured phenomenological investigations as ways to connect carefully elicited descriptions with physical measurements. Their role is to constrain a model, not to isolate an unconditioned substance.

A report depends on its protocol, memory, language, expectation and access. A later verbal account is already a transformation of an earlier episode. Shared instructions can affect both the report and physical measurements, so the two cannot simply be counted as wholly independent votes for an interpretation.

The monograph therefore proposes studying a joint law of physical measurements and reports under a declared protocol. Reported content, philosophical interpretation and physical conditions remain distinguishable within that joint model. Mixed or intermediate experiences should be described rather than forced into a binary choice between ordinary ego and completely contentless awareness.

That is an invitation to disciplined first-person research. It preserves the existential importance an episode can have for someone while keeping universal inferences open to public correction.

Chapter 3.4 explains the evidence model.

sections.title: The contemplative interpretation does not replace the laws
sections.html:
A0 states the source-awareness commitment; A1–A3 determine localized assignment, phenomenal organization and episode continuation under a supplied realization. A report of unchanged presence across altered content can be compatible with a continuing qualifying core. It does not prove that all physical structure stayed unchanged or that every organism has an uninterrupted experiential episode.

Nor does the persistence of reality establish personal survival. A3 specifies when a localized episode ends. The source does not demonstrate a person's migration back to source, knowledge beyond bodily death or numerical identity with every other perspective. Those stronger claims are not consequences of a noninjective readout or of a common-source ontology.

The positive interpretation remains substantial: the personal model need not exhaust what is meant by awareness, and changes in that model can change a lived world without erasing ordinary practical life. Turning that interpretation into an adequate account of actual vessels requires the same physical realization and phenomenal-comparison work as every other SPC-2 application.

Limits of the contemplative translation and its contribution to the resolution close the source's argument.

guides.title: SPC-2 and Other Theories of Consciousness
guides.description: A source-grounded comparison of SPC-2 with the philosophical and scientific programmes discussed in the publication, organized around their different explanatory commitments.

sections.title: Compare the questions and the commitments
sections.html:
SPC-2 combines a source-awareness premise with explicit laws for subject admission, phenomenal structure and temporal identity. Its distinctive proposal is this conjunction, not the invention of recurrence, predictive representation or fundamental experience in isolation. A useful comparison asks what each programme identifies with experience, how it selects a subject and what would count as evidence.

This guide follows the comparisons in the September 2026 monograph. It is not a comprehensive current review or a ranking of theories. The source distinguishes a mathematically determinate constitution from an empirically tested application: those are different achievements, and neither should be treated as a substitute for the other.

SPC-2's exact finite construction makes its dependencies visible. It also creates obligations to justify the realization and the constitutive laws. Explicitness is an advantage for inspection; it is not itself evidence that the resulting assignment is correct in nature.

Chapter 24.5 contains the edition's comparison and citations.

sections.title: Fundamental experience and the hard problem
sections.html:
The monograph treats Chalmers's hard-problem discussion as an antecedent that already allowed fundamental experience, structural coherence, organizational invariance and a double-aspect approach. It therefore does not claim to dissolve the problem by revealing that every earlier formulation assumed reductive materialism.

SPC-2 changes the proposed explanatory direction to manifestation. Awareness is primitive under A0; physically realized organization conditions local perspectives under A1–A3. That still leaves a hard burden: the laws must justify their particular assignments. A common source does not establish whether a given process has one perspective, many or none.

The sharp disagreement identified by the edition concerns structural completeness. Its reading of Chalmers leaves intrinsic qualitative character beyond structural description. A2 instead postulates no further manifested qualitative remainder once primitive presence and the complete nominated organization are fixed. This is a disagreement about a psychophysical premise. A proof about predictive quotients cannot decide it.

Chapter 1.1 gives the historical positioning; Chapter 24.2 explains the substantive choice.

sections.title: Integrated information theory
sections.html:
The edition describes IIT 4.0 as identifying experience with an irreducible cause–effect structure unfolded from a maximal substrate. It explicitly rejects the caricature that IIT is merely a scalar consciousness score. A fair comparison must address that structure and substrate selection rather than reduce the theory to one number.

SPC-2 selects qualifying maximal internal strongly connected cores using its realized joint-dependence organization, executable covering returns and native predictive distinctions. IIT's integrated cause–effect selection differs from that rule. A2's complete endogenous predictive instrument object also differs from the cause–effect structure identified in IIT.

The two programmes share concern with intrinsic organization, definite subjects and structured experience. Shared questions do not establish equivalent answers. The book supplies no general translation between their assignments and does not derive IIT's postulates from A0–A3.

An illuminating future comparison would need matched physical implementations, explicit modeling choices and identified cases in which assignments agree or diverge. Renaming one theory's object with the other's vocabulary would obscure the assumptions that actually need comparison.

The source's specific discussion appears in Chapter 24.5; SPC-2's own assignment is in A1 and A2.

sections.title: Global workspace and access
sections.html:
The monograph describes global neuronal workspace theory through access, global broadcasting and amplification. These concern how information becomes broadly available within a cognitive architecture. SPC-2 also treats access as physically important, while distinguishing access from primitive awareness and from the definition of every possible localized perspective.

This difference matters at the lower boundary. SPC-2 does not require adult human report, metacognition or a rich broadcasting architecture for every admitted case. Its formal A1 rule can admit certified minimal self-return processes. Its biological scene-forming interpretation cannot be used to silently add a stronger admission condition after that result.

The edition discusses the COGITATE adversarial collaboration as testing preregistered predictions of proposed biological implementations of workspace theory and IIT. It reports support for some predictions and challenges to important predictions of both. Those results concern specified neural accounts; they do not validate SPC-2 or settle source-awareness ontology.

The methodological lesson adopted is concrete: state competing commitments and the consequence of a failed prediction before examining outcomes. A theory needs a stable target for criticism as well as an explanation of successes.

See the source comparison and the distinction between access and scene organization.

sections.title: Predictive representation and AI indicators
sections.html:
The predictive mathematics has established antecedents, acknowledged in Chapter 16. SPC-2 uses an intrinsic-state quotient based on all admitted finite native tests and adds an explicit transition-congruence requirement. Its further move is psychophysical: A2 identifies the complete resulting structure with phenomenal organization.

Predictive sufficiency alone does not make that identification. A representation may capture all nominated future record laws without thereby proving presence or phenomenal adequacy. Nor is the actual intrinsic state an analyst's posterior belief. Those are essential distinctions when comparing the constitution with other uses of prediction.

For AI, the edition contrasts approaches that gather architectural indicators from several consciousness theories with SPC-2's single explicit admission, structure and continuity law. It also acknowledges biological-naturalist challenges to assuming an abstract computation preserves all consciousness-relevant properties. The book adopts no universal verdict about every artificial implementation from either comparison.

SPC-2's conditional substrate openness requires preservation of its full nominated realization, not merely matching output. Whether that realization omits an important biological property remains a question for the adequacy of the theory.

Chapter 16 acknowledges the mathematical antecedents; Chapter 22.1 frames the AI comparison.

sections.title: How to compare without inventing a winner
sections.html:
Three questions make comparisons more useful. First, what physical realization is being described, including its components, timing and admitted operations? Second, which constitutive identification connects that organization to experience? Third, what independent observation or philosophical consideration bears on the identification?

For SPC-2, a weak internal coupling can discontinuously change the exact subject count, and a genuinely certified simple register can qualify. Those consequences should remain visible in comparison. Adding a preferred complexity threshold or ignoring small internal edges may be a defensible new proposal, but it changes the current rule.

The programme also preserves all physical transcript probabilities when only its aspect interpretation is added. An otherwise identical physical reduct cannot be distinguished by those transcripts alone. Claims about realization adequacy and phenomenal correspondence can still be tested, but they should not be advertised as direct physical discrimination of transcript-identical ontologies.

A fair assessment therefore compares particular commitments and evidence, not labels such as mathematical, scientific or fundamental. SPC-2 contributes a clear conditional construction. Its status as a candidate remains tied to the justification of those commitments.

Weak-coupling sensitivity and conservativity are central comparison points.

guides.title: What Would Test the Shadow Consciousness Model?
guides.description: A practical reading of the edition's evidence programme: validate physical realizations, freeze phenomenal comparisons, expose failure conditions and respect transcript conservativity.

sections.title: Test the realization and the correspondence separately
sections.html:
SPC-2 can be assessed by testing proposed physical realizations and their fixed correspondence to independently elicited phenomenal relations. A model can fail to predict records, select an unjustified boundary or mismatch experience-related structure. These are substantive failure possibilities. The finite completion theorem does not settle them.

There is also a precise limitation. If the entire physical realization and every report law are held fixed, adding the source-aspect interpretation changes no physical transcript probabilities. A transcript-only experiment cannot then distinguish that interpretation from an otherwise identical physical account that denies it.

Useful testing begins by naming the claim. Is the target a component model, a sufficient descriptor, subject individuation, the A2 correspondence or the source-awareness premise? A positive result about one must not quietly become validation of all the others.

The conservativity theorem and Chapter 23.5 establish this division.

sections.title: First establish what the system does
sections.html:
A candidate realization must identify actual components, time scales, ports, preparation and intervention possibilities, resource updates and boundary conditions. Native operations cannot be whatever the analyst wishes were available. The model must account for memory that can return through an external interaction and for controller state that affects later operation.

Before assigning experience, test whether the model predicts the relevant physical records under held-out conditions. A fit to one preparation family is weaker than closure on every state in the nominated domain. Candidate projections that fail closure may need enlarged carriers or a history treatment. Failure of the representation is not yet a negative verdict about consciousness.

Realization selection is itself part of the research. The same bare transition kernel can admit different primitive factorizations, and a symmetry obstruction prevents a unique equivariant choice in a finite example. Components, native timing and internal route typing therefore need independent justification rather than the label “physical” alone.

The three realization roles and the selection obstruction define what must be supplied.

sections.title: Can the descriptor retain the target distinctions?
sections.html:
Choose an independently nominated target and a proposed physical descriptor. If conditions assigned the same descriptor value nevertheless differ in that target, no exact bridge through the descriptor can recover it. This is the practical meaning of fibre sufficiency: a representation cannot explain a distinction it has already erased.

The source proposes calibrated tests with declared tolerance, measurement error and regularity assumptions. For continuous descriptors, nearby rather than identical values require a bound on how rapidly the proposed bridge can change. A discrepancy beyond the allowed combination of proximity and error rejects that specified bridge.

The relevant constants and target cannot be chosen after seeing a failure merely to preserve the fit. Likewise, repeatedly training a new decoder for each mismatch would not test one fixed claim. A successful prediction on held-out interventions is more informative when the representation and calibration were frozen in advance.

For report distributions, compare the distributions rather than one coincident output. Physical instrument error, sampling uncertainty and model approximation have different origins and should remain identifiable in the analysis.

Chapter 23.2 gives the exact calibrated formulation.

sections.title: A2 needs an independent experience-facing target
sections.html:
